newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria oil refinery raises wages to avert strike.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria oil refinery raises wages to avert strike.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftohim has increased its workers' wages by 35 percent to avert a threatened strike, a trade union official said on Monday.
Dianko Dimov, leader of the independent Podkrepa trade union at the oil refinery, said by telephone that at this stage there were no conditions for a strike in Neftohim.
"After tense talks on Thursday and Friday, we reached an agreement with the plant's management for a 90 percent compensation for national inflation in November and December," Dimov told Reuters.

He added that from January 1 wages would be increased by 35 percent, meeting the economic demands of the trade union. Inflation is running at more than 300 percent a year and a wave of brief strikes have been held nationwide in the last two weeks against falling living standards and for early elections.
"We did not insist on a greater hike as we know what the financial situation of the plant and the country is," he said.

However local media said another trade union at the refinery, Promyana, had threatened to switch off some of the refineries' installations this week to support its demands that wages be pegged to the dollar.
Dimov said Podkrepa opposed such threats. "We know what such a move -- to switch off installations -- would mean for the country's economy and the responsibility we bear is great," he said.

Plant spokeswoman Tatyana Hadzhieva said the Promyana trade union had not given a warning to the management of any such action, as the labour code requires. Promyana leaders were not immediately available for comment.
Neftohim officials say the refinery has suffered huge losses because of the recent collapse of the lev, forcing up the cost of imported crude faster than the rise in Neftohim's domestic sales prices.
The Bulgarian lev traded near 737 per dollar on Monday amid expectations of a further fall.
The government usually revises energy prices each month in line with inflation, the exchange rate and world oil prices.
